title: Agents with real tools and no keys
subtitle: A governed gateway that lets AI agent teams use payments, email and social-publishing services with every action attributed and no credential in any agent

stats.label: vendor operations visible to managed agents, each rebuilt as my own tool
attribution and webhook delivery proven end to end

lede: I wanted AI agent teams to run small experimental businesses: take payments, send email, publish to social platforms. The moment you hand an agent a vendor API key you have three problems. The key leaks into logs. You cannot say afterwards which assignment created which customer or post. And the vendor's events, a payment, a reply, a bounce, have no way back to the team that caused them. I built one governed gateway between agents and vendors that solves all three. It exposes several hundred vendor operations to managed agents, every one attributed, with no agent ever holding a key. Each provider publishes an API for exactly these services.
quote: Attribution that might be silently dropped is worse than none.
evidence: Governed API integration for AI agents: one gateway exposing ~350 vendor operations, each rebuilt from the provider's API as my own tool, with 0 credentials held by any agent.
Identity architecture for AI agents: identity derived from the authenticated assignment, never from tool arguments, so an agent cannot act or bind a website for another business.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: durable accounting around every provider call, so a restart never repeats a charge or loses track of one.
Data attribution and provenance: attribution stamped into a vendor payload only where that operation and API version round-trips it, otherwise kept on my side; proven end to end on 2 hosts.
Webhook ingestion and routing: signed vendor events returned in frozen batches to the mailbox of the team lead whose assignment caused them.
author: Corey James
